findings.area: sampled Hebrew-only PDF source links / isolation claim
findings.finding: The source-link overlap does not affect only the HTML. hebrew.tex:375 puts two \OSScanLinkMargin calls (n5_medium and n7_medium) in one \pstart. \OSScanLinkMargin places each link at a fixed margin edge, at the height of the line it sits on. In hebrew-page-3.png the page break after עַל־ falls on the first printed line, so both links land on that line, and only one ↗ is visible there. The Hebrew-only PDF therefore has the same stacked, partly unreachable links as the Hebrew-only HTML. browser-qa.json, qa.json presentation_findings and veahavta_range_qa.json describe the problem as 'Hebrew-only HTML', and they say the PDF 'preserve[s] both sources'. That is true of the link annotations themselves, not of how they are presented.
findings.required_change: Change the open finding to cover the Hebrew-only PDF as well as the Hebrew-only HTML. Leave Hebrew-only PDF backlink presentation out of the requested approval, or fix it in the separate exporter PR. Then re-freeze the affected report hashes. This needs no change to the authoring code or the excerpt XML.

findings.finding: Scan 6 (box 100,1940–1280,2235) holds verse 5 through עַל־ in verse 6. Scan 8 (140,180–1250,490) holds לְבָבֶךָ: through וּבִשְׁעָרֶיךָ:. Scan 7 (100,1910–1300,2240) holds the ואהבת cue, then 'You shall love … in your children and'. Scan 9 (130,175–1270,475) holds 'speak of them … upon your gates.' The consonants, visible vowels, punctuation and English wording match the XML exactly. Nothing is omitted, added or reordered. The English ואהבת cue was correctly left out of the prayer text, as JLPTEI guidance requires. No translation was supplied for missing text.

Every cantillation mark in the XML matches accent_adjudications.json Q862–863 for verses 5–6 up to עַל־, including הַיּוֹ֖ם with tipcha on the vav (host index 2). It also matches user_adjudications_870_872.json for לְבָבֶֽךָ: through וּבִשְׁעָרֶֽיךָ:. That includes the double pashta in בְּבֵיתֶ֙ךָ֙, the meteg on the shuruq vav in וּֽבְשָׁכְבְּךָ֖, and the spelling מְזֻז֥וֹת with merkha on the second zayin. In scripture_ranges.json, the approved_working_s8 hash matches the snapshot_sha256 in s8_source_reading_approval.json. Where day 1 differs (הַיּ֖וֹם), it was correctly not used as wording evidence.

<j:divineName>יְהֹוָ֣ה</j:divineName> adds exactly one holam over the first he. The scan shows יְהוָ֣ה with no holam. The recipe records the holam as a normalization under edition convention user723 and does not claim it is printed, as SCAN_DIGITIZATION_INSTRUCTIONS:48–50 requires. It matches the day-1 convention. The semantic element survives into hebrew.tex.

Hebrew: the <pb n="3" facs="…/n7_medium.jpg"/> sits inside the verse 6 seg, right after עַל־, with no space (עַל־<pb/>לְבָבֶֽךָ:). English: the <pb n="3" facs="…/n8_medium.jpg"/> sits inside the verse 7 seg between 'and' and ' speak', keeping one word space. The zero-based leaves are correct: scans 6, 7, 8, 9 map to n5, n6, n7, n8. Page labels 2 and 3 are in @n and in biblScope from=2 to=3. Each verse seg starts with the right page: Hebrew n5, n5, n7, n7, n7; English n6, n6, n6, n8, n8. So verse 7 in Hebrew and verse 8 in English each keep their own source after the earlier break, as instructions 194–199 require.

Neither file has a div @corresp. The chapter milestone has n="6" and no corresp. Each verse milestone carries its exact canonical URN (deuteronomy/6/5 through 6/9), and the verse and chapter scopes are closed with terminators after verse 9 (JLPTEI-3 rule 3). The publication idno urn:x-opensiddur:text:bible:deuteronomy/6/5-/6/9@<project> uses the same range syntax as day 1, and no new canonical identity was created. Each verse milestone comes before its semantic seg@source, which follows JLPTEI-3:217–219. No citation note was invented.

draft_prayers.py handles range recipes with guarded alternates (--recipe plus a hash binding, rejecting an empty binding). Page-break events are local and add no spaces: spacing comes only from the surrounding strings. It rejects a non-positive page_break scan number, empty verse lists and duplicate verse URNs. A partial translation list gives only the verses actually listed. Missing counterparts are removed only through write_documents after every target validates. The tests cover each of these with invented data. tests.log shows 35 passed and 17 subtests passed. The single-verse path behaves as before (no seg@facs, div@corresp kept), which fits the claim that the regenerated output is byte-identical.

(a) If a page_break is the first item in a range verse's content, that verse's seg@facs still points to the previous page, even though all its words are on the new page. This happens because current_page only updates after append_content. A break between two verses cannot be expressed correctly yet. Either reject a leading page_break or use its page for the seg's starting facs. (b) Nothing checks that page-break scan numbers increase, or that printed_page_end equals the printed_page of the last page_break. biblScope/@to is copied straight from the recipe. Neither problem affects this excerpt.

parallel-page-3.png shows five aligned rows for verses 5–9 with matching verse numbers. Hebrew links: n5 at the verse 5 row, and n7 on the second line of the verse 6 row, at לְבָבֶךָ. English links: n6 at the verse 5 row, and n8 on the second line of the verse 7 row ('dren and speak'). No empty rows, no text copied from another verse, and no fallback for a missing translation. In the Hebrew-only PDF the text is continuous and correct, apart from the link presentation in F1.

qa.json records the expected quote counts: 5 for the Hebrew range, 1 for single verse 7, 10 for the parallel range and 2 for parallel single verse 7. It records source leaves n5/n7, n7, n5–n8 and n6/n7/n8. The only warnings are the expected fallback for the distinct machzor_expanded structural root, with no fallback for a missing translation. I did not re-run these probes.

scope_limitations: Read-only review: no tool to compute SHA-256, so I did not independently check the frozen artifact, input or processor hashes. I also could not check Unicode codepoint order byte by byte (for example mark order in בְּבֵיתֶ֙ךָ֙ or the shuruq meteg). I checked visible glyphs and that the XML matches the adjudication 'result' strings character for character.
I checked the fine cantillation at the resolution of the supplied crops, and I relied on the hash-bound adjudication records for marks too small to read.
The crops do not include the printed page numbers, so I accepted labels 2 and 3 as already-retained evidence without seeing them on the page.
Scan 9's English is bound from primary/s9.json, not an adjudicated working file. I checked its wording against the image myself, but that is not acceptance of the s9 reading.

I did not open the HTML or browser screenshots. I confirmed the HTML link collision only from the coordinates in browser-qa.json. I do not approve HTML presentation, and I do not approve Hebrew-only PDF backlink presentation (F1).
I sampled hebrew-page-3.png and parallel-page-3.png only. Not covered: whole source pages, the batch, full service order, conditional order and the expanded edition.
With F1 corrected in the QA record (no code or XML change), the authoring code, the exact excerpt XML, identity, alignment and the parallel PDF rows would qualify for approval as reviewed here.
